doc.summary: Non-blocking inline hint renderer for the LazyOwn cmd2 shell.
doc.description:
After each command executes, a single dim line is printed with the top-N
graph-based next-step suggestions derived from the graphify knowledge graph.
The GraphLoader caches by (path, mtime) so rendering is sub-millisecond after
the first graph load; subsequent calls return from memory.

Design notes:
- Zero coupling to cmd2, lazyown.py or Flask — this module is a pure renderer.
- The caller decides whether hints are enabled (reads payload.json flag).
- Output goes to stdout via rich so ANSI is handled correctly on all terminals.
- Commands on SKIP_COMMANDS never produce hints (noise-free UX).

name: render_inline_hints
signature: def render_inline_hints(advisor: GraphAdvisor, last_command: str, limit: int = 3, enabled: bool = True) -> None

doc.summary: Print a single dim hint line below the command output and return immediately.
doc.description:
The line format is:
    ↳ label_a · label_b · label_c

This renders between the command output and the next cmd2 prompt so it
never blocks the operator from typing the next command.

params.name: advisor
params.description: GraphAdvisor instance (reuses its internal mtime-keyed cache).

params.name: last_command
params.description: Raw command string that just executed (first token used).

params.name: limit
params.description: Maximum number of suggestions to display.

params.name: enabled
params.description: When False the function is a no-op. Controlled by the ``enable_inline_hints`` key in payload.json.

returns.description: None — side effect is at most one line written to stdout.

doc.summary: A next-step suggestion enriched with its justification and confidence.
doc.description:
The bare inline hint prints only command names, forcing the operator to
trust an unexplained list. This value object carries the *why* and *how
sure* so the hint line reads like advice rather than a menu.

attributes.name: verb
attributes.description: The command (or copy-paste preview) to run next.

attributes.name: confidence
attributes.description: Display confidence in ``[0, 100]`` derived from the fused recommendation score via :func:`confidence_from_score`.

attributes.name: reason
attributes.description: One-line English justification, stripped of the ``[source]`` provenance tag and truncated for the inline hint line.

attributes.name: sources
attributes.description: Names of the signals that agreed on this action.

doc.summary: Map an unbounded fused recommendation score to a 0-100 display confidence.
doc.description:
:class:`cli.recommendation.RecommendationEngine` produces scores that are
unbounded above because multiple agreeing signals add up, so a raw
percentage would be meaningless. This applies a saturating map
``100 * s / (s + K)`` where ``K`` (:data:`_CONFIDENCE_HALF_SCORE`) is the
score at which confidence reaches 50%. The map is monotonic — more signal
agreement yields higher confidence — and floors at 99 so the display never
claims a dishonest 100%.

params.name: score
params.description: The fused recommendation score. Negative values are floored at zero.

name: build_evidence_hints
signature: def build_evidence_hints(recommendations: Sequence[Any], limit: int) -> list[EvidenceHint]

doc.summary: Convert fused recommendations into display-ready evidence hints.
doc.description:
A recommendation without a usable verb or without a justification is
skipped so the operator never sees a bare, unexplained suggestion — an
explained shorter list beats a padded opaque one.

params.name: recommendations
params.description:
Ranked objects exposing ``action``, ``score``,
``reasons``, ``sources`` and optional ``command_preview`` (a
:class:`cli.recommendation.Recommendation` or any duck-typed
equivalent), best first.

params.name: limit
params.description: Maximum number of hints to return.

returns.description: Up to ``limit`` :class:`EvidenceHint` items preserving input order.

doc.summary: Print evidence-backed hint lines: verb, confidence, reason, provenance.
doc.description:
The first hint carries the ``↳`` arrow; the rest are indented to align, so
a glance reads as one ranked block of advice.

params.name: hints
params.description: The hints to render, already truncated and ranked.

returns.description: None — writes one dim line per hint to stdout.

doc.summary: Return the set of command names already executed this session.
doc.description:
Reads the CSV transcript and extracts the first token of the first
populated column (``tool``, ``command``, or ``name``). Shared by the
inline hint renderer, the tips engine, and any other surface that must
filter already-run commands out of its suggestions.

returns.description:
A set of command verbs, empty when the transcript is missing or
unreadable.

name: render_command_hints
signature: def render_command_hints(last_command: str, phase: str = '', sessions_dir: str = 'sessions', limit: int = 3, enabled: bool = True) -> None

doc.summary: Print phase-aware, history-filtered command hints after each step.
doc.description:
Uses kill-chain adjacency (``_KILL_CHAIN_NEXT``) first, then falls back
to phase priority (``_PHASE_PRIORITY``).  Commands already in the session
CSV are skipped so the hint is always forward-looking.

params.name: last_command
params.description: The command that just ran (first token used).

params.name: enabled
params.description: When False this is a no-op.

returns.description: None — prints at most one dim line.

name: command_hints
signature: def command_hints(last_command: str, phase: str = '', sessions_dir: str = 'sessions', limit: int = 3) -> list[str]

doc.summary: Return the top next-step command verbs without printing them.
doc.description:
Mirrors the logic of :func:`render_command_hints` but separates the
suggestion engine from the I/O side effect so other UI surfaces (the
persistent status bar in :mod:`cli.status_bar`, future TUI widgets)
can consume the exact same data the inline hints use.

params.name: last_command
params.description:
Raw command string that most recently executed.
Only the first token is considered. When empty or in
:data:`SKIP_COMMANDS` the adjacency lookup is skipped and the
phase priority table feeds the result.

params.name: phase
params.description: Current engagement phase identifier. Falls back to ``recon`` when empty.

params.name: sessions_dir
params.description: Path to ``sessions/`` used to filter out commands that already appear in the CSV transcript.

params.name: limit
params.description: Maximum number of verbs to return.

returns.description:
Ordered list of suggested command verbs, length ``<= limit``.
Returns an empty list when no candidates remain after filtering.
